title: Pericyte-Related Genetic Mechanisms of Blood-Brain Barrier Dysfunction in Dementia
content: Pericytes are essential components of the neurovascular unit (NVU), contributing to the maintenance of blood–brain barrier (BBB) integrity, the regulation of cerebral blood flow, and the modulation of neuroinflammatory responses. Accumulating evidence implicates pericyte dysfunction in the pathogenesis of several forms of dementia, particularly Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and vascular dementia (VaD). This review provides an overview of current knowledge regarding the role of pericytes in neurovascular dysfunction and cognitive decline, with particular emphasis on the genetic determinants of pericyte biology, including mutations and polymorphisms in genes such as PDGFRB, NOTCH3, COL4A1, and COL4A2. We examine the molecular mechanisms regulating pericyte function, their interactions with other NVU components, and the consequences of genetic alterations for BBB integrity and neurovascular and neuronal homeostasis. Particular attention is devoted to the contribution of BBB disruption to dementia pathophysiology and to emerging biomarkers of pericyte injury and BBB dysfunction, including soluble platelet-derived growth factor receptor beta (sPDGFRβ), the cerebrospinal fluid-to-serum albumin ratio (QAlb), and neurofilaments, as well as their potential associations with disease progression. Furthermore, we discuss emerging therapeutic approaches targeting pericyte dysfunction, including strategies to promote pericyte stabilization, modulate platelet-derived growth factor receptor (PDGFR) signaling, and implement gene- and epigenetic-based interventions. Overall, current evidence highlights the importance of pericyte-related genetic determinants and biomarkers as promising, yet still insufficiently characterized, aspects of dementia research. A better understanding of these mechanisms may facilitate the identification of early biomarkers, improve disease monitoring, and support the development of targeted therapeutic strategies aimed at preserving neurovascular integrity.
